security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives from code fences, package names, or inline examples. The confirmed risks are documented belt commands that submit arbitrary Python to a remote executor, outbound HTTP examples, and related skill installation commands. No prompt injection text was found, but the safety claim is not verifiable from this skill file.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary Python execution through an external CLI
remediation.suggestion: Document clear user confirmation requirements before running belt commands, especially when prompts include workspace files or secrets.

remediation.issue: Outbound network examples are enabled by default
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to avoid sending sensitive data to websites or APIs, and prefer allowlisted endpoints for examples.

remediation.issue: Sandbox safety is asserted without implementation evidence
remediation.suggestion: Link to auditable sandbox controls, data retention policies, and isolation guarantees for the inference.sh executor.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation commands are presented in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npx skills add commands from the related skills section.

content.user_title: Run Python Tasks in a Remote Sandbox
content.value_statement: Running Python from an AI assistant can require setup, libraries, and safe output handling. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code prompts to an inference.sh Python executor with common data, media, and web libraries.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python code through the inference.sh belt CLI.
Uses common libraries such as pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, requests, BeautifulSoup, Pillow, OpenCV, MoviePy, and trimesh.
Creates returned output files when code saves files in the outputs directory.
Supports web scraping and API request examples through Python HTTP libraries.
Runs CPU-only data, image, video, 3D, document, and automation tasks.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and a successful login.
Runs CPU-only tasks and does not provide GPU or dedicated machine learning libraries.
Timeouts are limited to one to 300 seconds.
Code and data are submitted to an external executor, so sensitive inputs need review.

use_cases.title: Analyze Small Datasets
use_cases.description: Process CSV-style data, calculate summary metrics, and save charts without local Python setup.

use_cases.title: Create Media Assets
use_cases.description: Generate images, short videos, PDFs, or 3D files using pre-installed Python libraries.

use_cases.title: Prototype Automation Scripts
use_cases.description: Run short Python scripts for API calls, file transformations, and repeatable utility tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Calculation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to run a short Python calculation. Print the result and explain what ran.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to analyze this table. Return summary statistics and save one chart in the outputs directory.

prompt_templates.title: Transform an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to resize and annotate the provided image. Save the processed image in the outputs directory.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Step Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using files and network calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch approved API data, transform it with pandas, save a report, and summarize the output files.

output_examples.input: Analyze a small sales table and create a chart.
output: A short written summary of total and average sales.
A chart file saved in the outputs directory.
A note listing the main libraries used.
A generated image file returned from the outputs directory.
A concise message confirming image dimensions and format.

output_examples.input: Fetch public profile data from an approved API.
output: A readable summary of selected fields.
A reminder that outbound requests were made to the approved endpoint.

best_practices: Review code before execution, especially when it reads files or makes network requests.
Save required artifacts in the outputs directory so they are returned reliably.
Use short timeouts first, then increase limits only for heavier jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not submit secrets, tokens, or private files unless the external executor is approved for them.
Do not run untrusted scraped code or commands copied from unknown sources.
Do not use this skill for GPU workloads or long-running services.

faq.question: Does this run Python locally?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses the inference.sh belt CLI to run code in an external executor.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it make network requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include requests-based web scraping and API calls.

faq.question: Where should generated files be saved?
faq.answer: Save files in the outputs directory so the executor can return them.

faq.question: Does it support GPU workloads?
faq.answer: No. The documented environment is CPU-only.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm that the code, inputs, and network endpoints are approved for an external execution service.
